html:
Long read · The national team

On Monday we told the stories of four players Thailand lost, or nearly lost. This is the list of the ones it should not. Twenty footballers with Thai heritage, from Malmö to Orange County, who could be wearing the shirt by the 2030 World Cup qualifiers. But a diaspora plan only works if it is built around a Thai core, and if the FA is prepared to pay for something as ordinary as Thai lessons.

Where we left off

The ones that got away set Felix Paschke, never asked and now retired at 23, beside Erawan Garnier, who was caught early, Stipe Ukich, whom New Zealand reached first, and Eric Kahl, who is still saying not yet. The lesson was that the federation waits, and that waiting costs players. We promised a list of who to call next. It ran long.

To build it we went through every post on @half_thailand.123, the account that has spent years tracking luk khrueng footballers around the world, and checked each player against Transfermarkt, club and federation sites and the local press. The result is our new directory of half-Thai and overseas Thai players: 139 men aged 15 and over, 11 of them already senior internationals. These are the twenty we would be on the phone to now.

How we chose

Each player has a Thai parent, or in two cases Thai heritage through a grandparent, which we have marked. Each is playing first-team football or is in a serious academy, and none is tied to another country by a competitive senior cap. Youth caps for Sweden, Switzerland or Belgium do not bind anyone; under FIFA's rules a player can switch once if he has not played more than three competitive senior matches for his first country, all before turning 21. We have left out players already capped by Thailand at senior level, and Kahl and Ukich, whom we covered on Monday. The order is urgency, not talent: who is closest to being lost.

Call now: ready for senior football
1

Adrian Skogmar

Malmö FF · Midfielder · age 20
Sweden U21

Two Allsvenskan titles and Champions League football before he turned 21. Reported to have met Anthony Hudson last December; his family say his focus is Sweden. The most talented player on this list, and the hardest sell.

2

Alexander Warneryd

Tromsø · Full-back · age 21
Sweden U21

His mother is from Prachinburi. Reported in March to have agreed to play for Thailand, but he was not in September's squad. If the deal is real, it needs a date on it.

3

Daniel Skaarud

Sandefjord · Winger · age 19
Norway U15 to U18

An Eliteserien debut for Lillestrøm at 15, a reported €1.2m move to Ajax, and now back in Norway's top flight on a deal to 2030. Thai mother, never approached as far as we can find.

4

Scott Constable

Arbroath, on loan from Dundee United · Right-back or holding midfielder · age 19
Scotland U19

Holds Thai citizenship and has said he would be happy to play for Thailand's under-23s. Scotland have capped him at youth level; that is not a reason to wait.

5

Aaron Gurd

Sydney Olympic, on loan from Sydney FC · Centre-back · age 25
No other caps

Spent last season at Kanchanaburi Power, where his Thai passport made him a local player. A senior centre-back with no other international ties, already proven in Thai League 1.

6

Theodor Agelin

Jerv, on loan from Sandefjord · Full-back · age 23
No other caps

Thai mother from Chiang Mai, Norwegian and Swedish passports, and no international football for anyone. Left-sided full-backs are not a position Thailand can afford to ignore.

7

Liam Källman

Vasalunds IF · Right-back · age 20
Sweden U16 to U18

A Hammarby academy product who now plays senior football in Sweden's third tier. He holds Thai citizenship already; the paperwork that held up others is not a problem here.

8

Norbu Lhakpa

FC Zürich U21 · Winger · age 18
Switzerland U19

Thai and Tibetan heritage, a Thai passport, and a goal in a Swiss Cup final at under-19 level. Switzerland are using him now. Thailand should be asking now.

Next window: the contested teenagers
9

Apolo Marinch

Orange County · Winger · born 2010
USA U15 camp

Signed a professional contract in the USL Championship in September 2025 and has played for the first team this year. The United States have already had him in camp. Of everyone here, he is the one most likely to be gone within two years.

10

Joey Waimer

Augsburg U19 · Centre-back · born 2009
UAE U17

Thai mother, German and Emirati passports, and a UAE under-17 cap that came against Thailand. Three countries want him; only one has not asked.

11

Lyndon Turrell

Leicester City U18 · Attacking midfielder · born 2009
Gibraltar U19

Has trained with Thailand's under-17s and scored against India, but has played for Gibraltar at every youth level. A Leicester academy player who has shown he wants Thailand deserves a clear plan.

12

Yanis Brisco

Charleroi U18 · Winger · born 2010
Belgium U15

A Belgian youth international with a Thai mother, back at Charleroi after two years at Club Brugge. Belgium's pathway is crowded; Thailand's is not.

13

Tanthai Theeten

Gent U18 · Left-back · born 2009
Belgium U16

Another Belgian youth international, in Gent's academy since 2023. His first name is Thai; the next call should be too.

14

Sven Spühler

FC Zürich U19 · Right-back · age 18
Switzerland U16

A Thai mother and a place in one of Switzerland's best academies. One Swiss youth cap so far, which means the door is wide open.

Keep close: in the system, or nearly
15

Silva Mexes

Leeds United U18 · Winger · born 2010
Thailand U17

Scored for Thailand at the 2025 AFC U17 Asian Cup and has just moved from Manchester United to Leeds. Also eligible for Wales and Zambia. Thailand has him; it needs to keep him.

16

Jake Fletcher

Leicester City U18 · Centre-forward · born 2008
Thailand U17

At Leicester since he was 11, three goals in his first four games this season and a Premier League 2 debut. Called up by Thailand at under-17 level; the under-20s should be next.

17

Orin Reinat

OH Leuven U23 · Defensive midfielder · age 18
No other caps

Through the Westerlo, Genk and Anderlecht academies to a Leuven contract until 2029. Belgian, Puerto Rican and Thai heritage. Nobody has capped him yet.

18

Jeremy Noser

FC Linth 04, on loan from Winterthur · Winger · born 2009
No other caps

Already playing senior football as a teenager, on loan in the Swiss fifth tier. Holds a Thai passport under the name Phumin.

19

Kevin Hahn

Holstein Kiel II · Midfielder · age 19
No other caps

Thai mother from Buriram, a hat-trick for Kiel's reserves this season, and reported interest from the Thailand under-20 coach. Interest is not a call-up.

20

Jordan Kinnavong

SF Baumberg U19 · Winger · age 18
Albania U17 friendlies

Thai and Lao heritage through his mother, two friendly caps for Albania, and on record saying he hopes to play for Thailand. The easiest yes on this list.

A Thai core, not a Thai shell

None of this is an argument for doing what Indonesia did. When Patrick Kluivert named a provisional squad in March 2025, 19 of the 30 players were naturalised (Databoks). It worked on the pitch; it beat Thailand in the FIFA ASEAN Cup final this month. But it is a national team assembled rather than grown, and Thailand has a league, an academy system and a football culture that deserve better than to be bypassed.

Our view is that Thailand should keep a core of players developed in Thailand by Thai clubs, the majority of any squad, and use the diaspora to add what the domestic game is not yet producing: a left-back here, a centre-back with Champions League minutes there. The Thai League gets a reason to keep investing in youth, the luk khrueng players arrive into a team with an identity rather than replacing it, and supporters still recognise the side as theirs. Every player above has a Thai parent. That is the line Thailand has drawn, and it is the right one.

Pay for the lessons

Integration is where the plan succeeds or fails, and it starts with language. Many of the players on this list grew up speaking Swedish, German, English or French at home. A dressing room, a team talk, a press conference and a terrace all happen in Thai. A player who cannot follow them is a guest, however good he is.

So here is a cheap, practical proposal: the FA should pay for Thai lessons for every mixed-heritage player it calls up who does not already speak the language, from his first youth camp. Online tutoring for the player and, for the younger ones, a parent; a short cultural induction at each camp; a buddy from the Thai-raised players in the squad. The cost is a rounding error next to a single scouting trip to Scandinavia. The return is a player who feels Thai in the room, not just on the passport.

The players themselves suggest the will is there. Jude Soonsup-Bell, capped by England at four youth levels, was asked whether he had needed persuading to choose Thailand.

"I didn't need convincing. I wanted to play for Thailand."
Jude Soonsup-Bell, to LiveScore

Wanting to play for a country and belonging in its dressing room are not the same thing, and the gap between them is exactly the kind of thing a federation can close with a little money and a little thought.

What to do on Monday morning

Make the calls on the first eight. Put the next six into the under-17 and under-20 camps before the end of the year, with flights paid and a Thai teacher waiting. Write to the clubs of the last six and keep them close. And keep the list current: our directory will be, and if you know a player we have missed, tell us. Monday's piece ended with a short list. This one is longer, and the clock is running on all of it.

Player details are from Transfermarkt, club and federation sites and the Instagram account @half_thailand.123, checked in October 2026; each name links to its profile in our directory, with sources. Ages are as of 13 October 2026. The views on squad composition and language lessons are Football Siam's.
